themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 165 THIS WEEK, a 255% jump from the 8-week baseline average of 46.5 per week (z-score: 6.75), suggesting rapid deterioration of road infrastructure across CD 405 that demands immediate investigation into whether winter damage, deferred maintenance, or construction activity is responsible.
evidence: 165 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 46.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.75 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Community board has repeatedly requested DOE and DEP capital funding for street/sewer infrastructure
415 total DOB permits filed in last 90 days (323 alterations) could indicate construction-related damage
reporting_angles: Tour streets in Ridgewood, Glendale, Middle Village with DOT to document specific potholes, buckled pavement, and timeline for repairs
Investigate whether recent construction permits (alteration filings) have triggered street degradation complaints; cross-reference complaint addresses with permit locations

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.6 per week (380% spike, z-score: 4.91), marking a potential public health concern in a district with active food service establishments that warrants DOH coordination and source identification.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average
Z-score of 4.91 indicates high statistical significance
Small absolute numbers (3 complaints) suggest this may be a localized outbreak rather than district-wide pattern
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DOH to obtain the specific food service establishments cited in the 3 complaints; determine if common food source or venue
Reach out to complainants to identify shared restaurants, caterers, or food vendors and timing of illness onset

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicle Surge
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints peaked 2 weeks ago at 44, more than double the 8-week baseline of 21.5 per week (105% spike, z-score: 4.85), pointing to a possible dumping problem or enforcement gap that affects neighborhood aesthetics and public safety.
evidence: 44 derelict vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 21.5 weekly average
Abandoned vehicles are a top 90-day complaint type overall (933 total), but recent spike suggests acceleration
reporting_angles: Map the geographic concentration of the 44 derelict vehicle complaints from 2 weeks ago—are they clustered in specific blocks or wards, suggesting organized dumping?
Interview NYPD and DSNY about enforcement response; determine if complaints have been resolved and what timeline exists for vehicle removal

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Calls Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police complaints surged to 26 two weeks ago, a 136% increase from the 11.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.42), suggesting a possible crime or quality-of-life incident cluster that may signal emerging neighborhood safety concerns.
evidence: 26 non-emergency police complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 11.0 weekly average
Safety complaints also spiked 220% to 10 complaints 2 weeks ago (vs. 3.1 baseline), suggesting convergent signal
reporting_angles: Request NYPD complaint logs and incident reports from 2 weeks ago to categorize what types of non-emergency calls (e.g., harassment, trespassing, vandalism) drove the spike
Interview 110th Precinct commanding officer about whether they observed unusual activity or crime patterns in that week

themes_detail.label: Building Code & Plumbing Issues
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints jumped 153% to 25 last week (vs. 9.9 baseline, z-score: 5.08) and general construction/plumbing complaints rose 68% to 22 (vs. 13.1 baseline), suggesting potential code violations or maintenance failures linked to the 415 active DOB permits, and reflecting the community board's longstanding request for additional building inspectors.
evidence: Building/use complaints: 25 last week vs. 9.9 weekly average (153% spike, z-score: 5.08)
Construction/plumbing complaints: 22 last week vs. 13.1 weekly average (68% spike, z-score: 4.25)
Community board has formally requested additional DOB building inspectors in budget submissions (recurring ask)
415 total DOB permits filed in past 90 days with 323 alteration permits indicate active construction activity district-wide
reporting_angles: Interview DOB and community board leadership on the gap between permit volume (415 filings) and available inspection capacity; quantify the inspector shortage
Cross-reference the 25 building/use complaints from last week with active permits to identify which projects are generating the most violations or resident complaints
